title: Second identities
text: Ask a young designer what they do, and the answer may {{1}} three jobs and a podcast. The portfolio career — several part-time strands rather than one employer — was once a euphemism for {{2}}; it is becoming a deliberate {{3}}. Technology {{4}} much of the shift: platforms match spare hours to spare demand, and the same laptop that once {{5}} a single salary can invoice three clients. Employers, for their part, increasingly {{6}} specialists for projects rather than keeping every skill on staff. The gains are real: multiple incomes {{7}} risk, varied work builds unusual combinations of skills, and autonomy is the benefit workers consistently {{8}} most highly. The costs are quieter: no colleagues by default, no employer pension, and an admin day that never arrives. The portfolio career, in other words, is not a lifestyle hack but a new employment contract, unwritten — and everyone involved is still negotiating its terms.

gaps.explanation: 'the answer may cover three jobs and a podcast' — extend across them; conceal = hide.
'a euphemism for unemployment' — the polite cover for having no work; undercurrent = a hidden feeling or flow.
'becoming a deliberate strategy' — a chosen plan; stratification = layering, syndication = selling content to outlets.
'technology underlies much of the shift' — lies beneath and supports it; undermine = weaken.
'the laptop that once earned a single salary' — brought the money in; yearn = long for, spurn = reject.
'employers hire specialists for projects' — engage them temporarily; acquire = obtain.
'multiple incomes spread risk' — distribute it so no single failure is fatal; spur = encourage.
'the benefit workers value most highly' — the finite verb is needed after 'workers'; valuable is the adjective and valuation the noun.
